title: Sections of the inverse image to a directed limit of spectral spaces over a quasi-compact open are a colimit
statement: Let $I$ be a directed set (nonempty, any two elements have a common upper bound), let $(X_i)_{i\in I}$ be spectral spaces [def-weil-spectral-space] and for $i\le i'$ let $f_{ii'}:X_{i'}\to X_i$ be spectral maps (continuous, with $f_{ii'}^{-1}(W)$ quasi-compact for every quasi-compact open $W\subseteq X_i$), with $f_{ii}=\mathrm{id}$ and $f_{ii'}\circ f_{i'i''}=f_{ii''}$ for $i\le i'\le i''$. Let $X$ be a topological space with continuous maps $p_i:X\to X_i$, $f_{ii'}\circ p_{i'}=p_i$, which is a limit of the system in the category of topological spaces (the map $x\mapsto(p_i(x))_i$ is a bijection of $X$ onto $\{(x_i)\in\prod_iX_i: f_{ii'}(x_{i'})=x_i\text{ for }i\le i'\}$ and the topology of $X$ is the coarsest for which all $p_i$ are continuous). For a continuous map $h$ let $h^{-1}$ be the inverse image of sheaves of sets with unit $\eta^h$ on sections, as in [def-weil-pbc-topological-inverse-image] (2), (3) with values in sets, and for continuous maps $h,h'$ let $c:h'^{-1}h^{-1}\xrightarrow{\sim}(h\circ h')^{-1}$ be the isomorphism of [lem-weil-pbc-sets-inverse-image-composition]. Fix $i\in I$, a sheaf of sets $\mathcal G$ on $X_i$ and a quasi-compact open $U_i\subseteq X_i$. For $i'\ge i$ put $\mathcal G_{i'}=f_{ii'}^{-1}\mathcal G$ and $U_{i'}=f_{ii'}^{-1}(U_i)$ (so $p_{i'}^{-1}(U_{i'})=p_i^{-1}(U_i)$), let $\rho_{i'}:\mathcal G_{i'}(U_{i'})\to(p_i^{-1}\mathcal G)(p_i^{-1}U_i)$ be $c_{\mathcal G}\circ\eta^{p_{i'}}_{\mathcal G_{i'},U_{i'}}$ with $c:p_{i'}^{-1}f_{ii'}^{-1}\mathcal G\xrightarrow{\sim}(f_{ii'}\circ p_{i'})^{-1}\mathcal G=p_i^{-1}\mathcal G$, and for $i\le i'\le i''$ let $\rho_{i''i'}:\mathcal G_{i'}(U_{i'})\to\mathcal G_{i''}(U_{i''})$ be $c_{\mathcal G}\circ\eta^{f_{i'i''}}_{\mathcal G_{i'},U_{i'}}$ with $c:f_{i'i''}^{-1}f_{ii'}^{-1}\mathcal G\xrightarrow{\sim}f_{ii''}^{-1}\mathcal G$. Then (a) $\rho_{i'i'}=\mathrm{id}$, $\rho_{i''}\circ\rho_{i''i'}=\rho_{i'}$ and $\rho_{i'''i''}\circ\rho_{i''i'}=\rho_{i'''i'}$ for $i\le i'\le i''\le i'''$; (b) every $s\in(p_i^{-1}\mathcal G)(p_i^{-1}U_i)$ equals $\rho_{i'}(t)$ for some $i'\ge i$ and some $t\in\mathcal G_{i'}(U_{i'})$; (c) if $t,t'\in\mathcal G_{i'}(U_{i'})$ and $\rho_{i'}(t)=\rho_{i'}(t')$, then $\rho_{i''i'}(t)=\rho_{i''i'}(t')$ for some $i''\ge i'$. In other words $(p_i^{-1}\mathcal G)(p_i^{-1}U_i)=\varinjlim_{i'\ge i}(f_{ii'}^{-1}\mathcal G)(f_{ii'}^{-1}U_i)$.

proof.text: *Step 1 (the limit and the opens).* By [lem-weil-pbc-spectral-directed-limit-spectral] $X$ is a spectral space and every $p_k$ is spectral. Hence: for $j\le k$ and a quasi-compact open $W\subseteq X_j$, $f_{jk}^{-1}(W)$ is a quasi-compact open of $X_k$ and $p_k^{-1}(f_{jk}^{-1}W)=(f_{jk}p_k)^{-1}(W)=p_j^{-1}(W)$ is a quasi-compact open of $X$; in particular $U_{i'}=f_{ii'}^{-1}(U_i)$ is a quasi-compact open of $X_{i'}$ and $p_{i'}^{-1}(U_{i'})=p_i^{-1}(U_i)$ is a quasi-compact open of $X$. The quasi-compact opens of $X$ and of each $X_k$ form a basis and the intersection of two of them is quasi-compact [def-weil-spectral-space]. Cofinality: for $j\in I$ put $J=\{k\in I:k\ge j\}$ (directed and nonempty); if $(z_k)_{k\in J}$ satisfies $z_k\in X_k$ and $f_{kk'}(z_{k'})=z_k$ for $k\le k'$ in $J$, then there is $x\in X$ with $p_k(x)=z_k$ for all $k\in J$. Indeed, for $m\in I$ choose $k\in J$ with $k\ge m$ and put $x_m=f_{mk}(z_k)$; this does not depend on $k$ (for two choices $k,k'$ take $k''\in J$ above both: $f_{mk}(z_k)=f_{mk}f_{kk''}(z_{k''})=f_{mk''}(z_{k''})$, the same for $k'$), it equals $z_m$ for $m\in J$, and $f_{mm'}(x_{m'})=x_m$ for $m\le m'$ (compute both with one $k\ge m'$); as $X$ is the limit, there is $x\in X$ with $p_m(x)=x_m$ for all $m$.

proof.text: *Step 2 (the maps $\rho^W$).* For $i\le j\le k$ write $\mathcal G_j=f_{ij}^{-1}\mathcal G$ and, for an open $W\subseteq X_j$, let $\rho^W_{kj}=c_{\mathcal G}\circ\eta^{f_{jk}}_{\mathcal G_j,W}:\mathcal G_j(W)\to\mathcal G_k(f_{jk}^{-1}W)$ with $c:f_{jk}^{-1}f_{ij}^{-1}\mathcal G\xrightarrow{\sim}(f_{ij}f_{jk})^{-1}\mathcal G=\mathcal G_k$, and $\rho^W_j=c_{\mathcal G}\circ\eta^{p_j}_{\mathcal G_j,W}:\mathcal G_j(W)\to(p_i^{-1}\mathcal G)(p_j^{-1}W)$ with $c:p_j^{-1}f_{ij}^{-1}\mathcal G\xrightarrow{\sim}(f_{ij}p_j)^{-1}\mathcal G=p_i^{-1}\mathcal G$ [lem-weil-pbc-sets-inverse-image-composition] (the equalities $f_{ij}f_{jk}=f_{ik}$, $f_{ij}p_j=p_i$ hold on the nose). Then $\rho_{i'}=\rho^{U_{i'}}_{i'}$ and $\rho_{i''i'}=\rho^{U_{i'}}_{i''i'}$. Since $\eta^h_{\mathcal K}:\mathcal K\to h_*h^{-1}\mathcal K$ is a morphism of sheaves [def-weil-pbc-topological-inverse-image] (3) and $c$ is a morphism of sheaves, $\rho^W_{kj}$ and $\rho^W_j$ commute with restriction: for opens $W'\subseteq W$ and $t\in\mathcal G_j(W)$, $\rho^{W'}_{kj}(t|_{W'})=\rho^W_{kj}(t)|_{f_{jk}^{-1}W'}$ and $\rho^{W'}_j(t|_{W'})=\rho^W_j(t)|_{p_j^{-1}W'}$.

proof.text:
*Step 3 (the isomorphisms $c$ are compatible with triple composites).* Let $A\xrightarrow{q}B\xrightarrow{b}C\xrightarrow{a}D$ be continuous maps, $\mathcal G$ a sheaf of sets on $D$, and write $c^{h,g}:h^{-1}g^{-1}\to(gh)^{-1}$ for the isomorphisms of [lem-weil-pbc-sets-inverse-image-composition]. Claim: for every open $V\subseteq C$ and $t\in(a^{-1}\mathcal G)(V)$,
$$c^{q,ab}_{\mathcal G}\bigl(\eta^q_{(ab)^{-1}\mathcal G,b^{-1}V}(c^{b,a}_{\mathcal G}(\eta^b_{a^{-1}\mathcal G,V}(t)))\bigr)=c^{bq,a}_{\mathcal G}\bigl(\eta^{bq}_{a^{-1}\mathcal G,V}(t)\bigr).\qquad(*)$$
(i) For a continuous $h:S\to T$ and sheaves $\mathcal K$ on $T$, $\mathcal F$ on $S$, the adjunction bijection of [def-weil-pbc-topological-inverse-image] (3), $\psi\mapsto\psi\circ\theta\mapsto h_*(\psi\theta)\circ i_{\mathcal K}=h_*\psi\circ\eta^h_{\mathcal K}$, shows that a morphism $\psi:h^{-1}\mathcal K\to\mathcal F$ is determined by the maps $\psi_{h^{-1}V}\circ\eta^h_{\mathcal K,V}$ ($V\subseteq T$ open), and that every morphism $\mathcal K\to h_*\mathcal F$ is of this form. (ii) $\eta^h$ is natural: for $u:\mathcal K\to\mathcal K'$, $\eta^h_{\mathcal K',V}\circ u_V=(h^{-1}u)_{h^{-1}V}\circ\eta^h_{\mathcal K,V}$ (unit of an adjunction, same node). (iii) Let $\Phi=c^{q,ab}_{\mathcal G}\circ q^{-1}(c^{b,a}_{\mathcal G})$ and $\Psi=c^{bq,a}_{\mathcal G}\circ c^{q,b}_{a^{-1}\mathcal G}$, two morphisms $q^{-1}b^{-1}a^{-1}\mathcal G\to(abq)^{-1}\mathcal G$. Applying (i) for $q$, then for $b$ to $q_*\psi\circ\eta^q$, then for $a$, a morphism $\psi:q^{-1}b^{-1}a^{-1}\mathcal G\to\mathcal F$ is determined by the maps $s\mapsto\psi(\eta^q(\eta^b(\eta^a_{\mathcal G,W}(s))))$, $s\in\mathcal G(W)$, $W\subseteq D$ open (sections over $a^{-1}W$, $(ab)^{-1}W$, $(abq)^{-1}W$). On these, by (ii) with $u=c^{b,a}_{\mathcal G}$ and the defining property of $c$ (applied to $c^{b,a}$, then $c^{q,ab}$): $\Phi(\eta^q\eta^b\eta^a s)=c^{q,ab}(\eta^q(c^{b,a}(\eta^b\eta^as)))=c^{q,ab}(\eta^q(\eta^{ab}s))=\eta^{abq}(s)$; and by the defining property of $c^{q,b}$ for the sheaf $a^{-1}\mathcal G$ and the section $\eta^a(s)$, then of $c^{bq,a}$: $\Psi(\eta^q\eta^b\eta^as)=c^{bq,a}(\eta^{bq}(\eta^as))=\eta^{abq}(s)$. Hence $\Phi=\Psi$. (iv) By (ii), the left side of $(*)$ is $\Phi(\eta^q(\eta^b t))=\Psi(\eta^q(\eta^bt))=c^{bq,a}(c^{q,b}_{a^{-1}\mathcal G}(\eta^q\eta^bt))=c^{bq,a}(\eta^{bq}t)$, the last equality by the defining property of $c^{q,b}$ for $a^{-1}\mathcal G$ and $t$.

proof.text: *Step 4 (the system identities; part (a)).* For $i\le j\le k\le l$ and an open $W\subseteq X_j$: ($\alpha$) $\rho^{f_{jk}^{-1}W}_k\circ\rho^W_{kj}=\rho^W_j$: this is $(*)$ of Step 3 with $a=f_{ij}$, $b=f_{jk}$, $q=p_k$, $V=W$ (then $ab=f_{ik}$, $bq=p_j$). ($\beta$) $\rho^{f_{jk}^{-1}W}_{lk}\circ\rho^W_{kj}=\rho^W_{lj}$: $(*)$ with $a=f_{ij}$, $b=f_{jk}$, $q=f_{kl}$. ($\gamma$) $\rho^W_{jj}=\mathrm{id}$: here $f_{jj}=\mathrm{id}$ and $\mathrm{id}_*\mathcal K=\mathcal K$, so by Step 3 (i) there is a morphism $\varepsilon:\mathrm{id}^{-1}\mathcal G_j\to\mathcal G_j$ with $\varepsilon_V\circ\eta^{\mathrm{id}}_{\mathcal G_j,V}=\mathrm{id}$ for all $V$; then $\varepsilon(\eta^{\mathrm{id}}(\eta^{f_{ij}}_{\mathcal G,V}(s)))=\eta^{f_{ij}}_{\mathcal G,V}(s)$, which is the property characterizing $c^{\mathrm{id},f_{ij}}_{\mathcal G}$ in [lem-weil-pbc-sets-inverse-image-composition] (uniqueness clause), so $c=\varepsilon$ and $\rho^W_{jj}(t)=\varepsilon(\eta^{\mathrm{id}}(t))=t$. With $W=U_{i'}$, $j=i'$, $k=i''$, $l=i'''$ (Step 2) this is (a): $\rho_{i'i'}=\mathrm{id}$, $\rho_{i''}\circ\rho_{i''i'}=\rho_{i'}$, $\rho_{i'''i''}\circ\rho_{i''i'}=\rho_{i'''i'}$.

proof.text: *Step 5 (germs).* For $i\le j\le k$, an open $W\subseteq X_j$ and $t,t'\in\mathcal G_j(W)$: for $y\in f_{jk}^{-1}(W)$, $(\rho^W_{kj}t)_y=(\rho^W_{kj}t')_y$ iff $t_{f_{jk}(y)}=t'_{f_{jk}(y)}$; for $x\in p_j^{-1}(W)$, $(\rho^W_jt)_x=(\rho^W_jt')_x$ iff $t_{p_j(x)}=t'_{p_j(x)}$ (stalks and germs of sheaves of sets, colimits [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] over the open neighbourhoods). Proof, for $h=f_{jk}$ or $h=p_j$ and a point $y$ of its source: by [lem-weil-pbc-sets-inverse-image-stalk] there is a bijection $\beta:(\mathcal G_j)_{h(y)}\to(h^{-1}\mathcal G_j)_y$ with $\beta(t_{h(y)})=(\eta^h_{\mathcal G_j,W}(t))_y$. The isomorphism of sheaves $c$ of Step 2 [lem-weil-pbc-sets-inverse-image-composition] commutes with restrictions, so by the universal property of the stalk colimit it induces a map $c_y$ on stalks with $c_y(u_y)=(c(u))_y$; $(c^{-1})_y$ is inverse to it (both composites fix every germ, and every element of a stalk is a germ [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-sets-elementwise] (1)). Hence $(\rho t)_y=c_y(\beta(t_{h(y)}))$ with $c_y\circ\beta$ bijective.

proof.text: *Step 6 (the set where two sections differ).* Let $k\ge i$, $W\subseteq X_k$ a quasi-compact open, $a,b\in\mathcal G_k(W)$ and $Z=\{y\in W:a_y\ne b_y\}$. (i) $W\setminus Z$ is open: if $a_y=b_y$, then by [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-sets-elementwise] (3) for the stalk colimit at $y$ (directed set of open neighbourhoods) there is an open $V$ with $y\in V\subseteq W$ and $a|_V=b|_V$, so $a_{y'}=b_{y'}$ for all $y'\in V$. (ii) $Z$ is closed in the constructible topology [def-weil-pbc-constructible-topology] of $X_k$: the open set $W\setminus Z$ of $X_k$ is a union of quasi-compact opens [def-weil-spectral-space], each open in the constructible topology, so $X_k\setminus(W\setminus Z)$ is closed in it; $X_k\setminus W$ belongs to the subbase, so $W$ is closed in it; and $Z=W\cap(X_k\setminus(W\setminus Z))$.

proof.text: *Step 8 (local form of a section over $p_i^{-1}U_i$).* Let $s\in(p_i^{-1}\mathcal G)(p_i^{-1}U_i)$. Claim: there are $n\ge1$ and, for $l=1,\dots,n$, quasi-compact opens $W_l\subseteq X$ and $V_l\subseteq U_i$ of $X_i$ and $u_l\in\mathcal G(V_l)$ with $W_l\subseteq p_i^{-1}(V_l)$, $\bigcup_lW_l=p_i^{-1}(U_i)$ and $s|_{W_l}=\eta^{p_i}_{\mathcal G,V_l}(u_l)|_{W_l}$. Fix $x\in p_i^{-1}(U_i)$, $y=p_i(x)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-sets-inverse-image-stalk] the map $\mathcal G_y\to(p_i^{-1}\mathcal G)_x$, $u_y\mapsto(\eta^{p_i}_{\mathcal G,V}(u))_x$, is bijective, so $s_x=(\eta^{p_i}_{\mathcal G,V}(u))_x$ for some open $V\ni y$ and $u\in\mathcal G(V)$. Choose a quasi-compact open $V'$ with $y\in V'\subseteq V\cap U_i$ [def-weil-spectral-space]; as $\eta^{p_i}$ commutes with restriction, $(\eta^{p_i}_{\mathcal G,V'}(u|_{V'}))_x=s_x$. By [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-sets-elementwise] (2) for the stalk at $x$ there is an open $O\ni x$, $O\subseteq p_i^{-1}(V')$, with $s|_O=\eta^{p_i}_{\mathcal G,V'}(u|_{V'})|_O$; choose a quasi-compact open $W_x$ with $x\in W_x\subseteq O$ ($X$ is spectral, Step 1). The $W_x$ cover the quasi-compact set $p_i^{-1}(U_i)$ (Step 1), so finitely many do; if $p_i^{-1}(U_i)=\emptyset$ take $n=1$, $W_1=V_1=\emptyset$ and $u_1$ the unique section of the sheaf $\mathcal G$ over $\emptyset$.

proof.text: *Step 9 (descending the covering; Tag 0A30).* Claim: there are $j\ge i$ and quasi-compact opens $W_{l,j}\subseteq X_j$ with $p_j^{-1}(W_{l,j})=W_l$, $W_{l,j}\subseteq f_{ij}^{-1}(V_l)$ and $\bigcup_lW_{l,j}=U_j$. By [lem-weil-pbc-spectral-limit-descend-opens] (1) there are $j_l\in I$ and quasi-compact opens $W'_l\subseteq X_{j_l}$ with $p_{j_l}^{-1}(W'_l)=W_l$. Take $j_0\ge i,j_1,\dots,j_n$ and $W''_l=f_{j_lj_0}^{-1}(W'_l)$, quasi-compact open with $p_{j_0}^{-1}(W''_l)=W_l\subseteq p_i^{-1}(V_l)$ (Step 1). By part (2) of the same node there are $k_l\ge j_0$ with $f_{j_0k_l}^{-1}(W''_l)\subseteq f_{ik_l}^{-1}(V_l)$; for $k\ge k_1,\dots,k_n$, applying $f_{k_lk}^{-1}$, $W'''_l:=f_{j_0k}^{-1}(W''_l)\subseteq f_{ik}^{-1}(V_l)$, quasi-compact open with $p_k^{-1}(W'''_l)=W_l$. Since $p_k^{-1}(U_k)=p_i^{-1}(U_i)=\bigcup_lp_k^{-1}(W'''_l)$, part (3) gives $j\ge k$ with $f_{kj}^{-1}(U_k)=\bigcup_lf_{kj}^{-1}(W'''_l)$. Put $W_{l,j}=f_{kj}^{-1}(W'''_l)$: then $\bigcup_lW_{l,j}=U_j$, $W_{l,j}\subseteq f_{ij}^{-1}(V_l)$ and $p_j^{-1}(W_{l,j})=W_l$.

proof.text: *Step 10 (sections at level $j$).* Let $\sigma_l=\eta^{f_{ij}}_{\mathcal G,V_l}(u_l)|_{W_{l,j}}\in\mathcal G_j(W_{l,j})$. By Step 2, $\rho^{W_{l,j}}_j(\sigma_l)=\rho^{f_{ij}^{-1}V_l}_j(\eta^{f_{ij}}_{\mathcal G,V_l}(u_l))|_{W_l}=c_{\mathcal G}\bigl(\eta^{p_j}_{\mathcal G_j,f_{ij}^{-1}V_l}(\eta^{f_{ij}}_{\mathcal G,V_l}(u_l))\bigr)|_{W_l}=\eta^{p_i}_{\mathcal G,V_l}(u_l)|_{W_l}=s|_{W_l}$, by the defining property of $c$ in [lem-weil-pbc-sets-inverse-image-composition] ($f_{ij}p_j=p_i$) and Step 8. For $l,l'$ the set $W_{ll'}=W_{l,j}\cap W_{l',j}$ is a quasi-compact open of $X_j$ [def-weil-spectral-space] with $p_j^{-1}(W_{ll'})=W_l\cap W_{l'}$, and by Step 2 $\rho^{W_{ll'}}_j(\sigma_l|_{W_{ll'}})=s|_{W_l\cap W_{l'}}=\rho^{W_{ll'}}_j(\sigma_{l'}|_{W_{ll'}})$.

proof.text: *Step 11 (gluing; part (b)).* By Step 7 for each pair $(l,l')$ there is $k_{ll'}\ge j$ with $\rho^{W_{ll'}}_{k_{ll'}j}(\sigma_l|_{W_{ll'}})=\rho^{W_{ll'}}_{k_{ll'}j}(\sigma_{l'}|_{W_{ll'}})$; take $k\ge$ all $k_{ll'}$; by Step 4 ($\beta$) the equality holds with $k$ in place of $k_{ll'}$. Put $\tau_l=\rho^{W_{l,j}}_{kj}(\sigma_l)\in\mathcal G_k(f_{jk}^{-1}W_{l,j})$. By Step 2, $\tau_l$ and $\tau_{l'}$ agree on $f_{jk}^{-1}(W_{ll'})$, and the $f_{jk}^{-1}(W_{l,j})$ cover $f_{jk}^{-1}(U_j)=U_k$. Since $\mathcal G_k=f_{ik}^{-1}\mathcal G$ is a sheaf [def-weil-pbc-topological-inverse-image] (3), [def-weil-pbc-sheafification], there is $\tau\in\mathcal G_k(U_k)$ with $\tau|_{f_{jk}^{-1}W_{l,j}}=\tau_l$. Then, by Step 2, Step 4 ($\alpha$) and Step 10, $\rho_k(\tau)|_{W_l}=\rho^{f_{jk}^{-1}W_{l,j}}_k(\tau_l)=\rho^{W_{l,j}}_j(\sigma_l)=s|_{W_l}$ (note $p_k^{-1}f_{jk}^{-1}W_{l,j}=W_l$). As the $W_l$ cover $p_i^{-1}(U_i)$ and $p_i^{-1}\mathcal G$ is a sheaf, $\rho_k(\tau)=s$. This is (b) with $i'=k$.

proof.text: *Step 12 (the colimit).* The set $\{i'\in I:i'\ge i\}$ is directed, hence a filtered category [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]; by (a) $i'\mapsto\mathcal G_{i'}(U_{i'})$ with the maps $\rho_{i''i'}$ is a functor and the $\rho_{i'}$ form a cocone, so they induce a map $\varinjlim_{i'\ge i}\mathcal G_{i'}(U_{i'})\to(p_i^{-1}\mathcal G)(p_i^{-1}U_i)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-sets-elementwise] (1) and (3) every element of the colimit is the image of some $t\in\mathcal G_{i'}(U_{i'})$, and two elements $t,t'\in\mathcal G_{i'}(U_{i'})$ have the same image iff $\rho_{i''i'}(t)=\rho_{i''i'}(t')$ for some $i''\ge i'$ (two elements given at different indices are first moved to a common upper index by (a)). Hence the map is surjective by (b) and injective by (c) and (a): it is bijective.
